domain: Sharp photon inputs n_k in {0,1}, classical initial memory, length <=3; optical-only bin preparation and retained memory
embedding: For input word n, prepare the product Fock vector with occupations n_k at fresh labelled detector ports p_k=2+3k, every other mode vacuum. Total photon number may be 0,1,2,3. Tensor with the classical R/D memory mixture.
operation_map: At bin k apply the same separately labelled local source Kraus instrument at p_k, identity on all spectator modes. Destroy only the current optical input, retain memory and all future optical inputs. Do not apply a cavity round in this detector-only presentation.
history_comparison: Local source preparation/instrument route and preprepared multi-bin Fock route have the same unnormalized memory populations and complete word probabilities at every prefix; unused future modes remain sharp spectators.
resource_comparison: Expected initial photon number equals final spectator photon number plus cumulative absorbed photon number, including click and no-click loss. One photon is consumed for every bin with n_k=1, regardless of whether it clicks. Ready/dead populations remain a separate ledger.
composition: Events retain bin/port, outcome, occurrence/predecessor IDs and model clock version. A segment takes an explicit start bin and concatenates only with the matching next bin. Empty segment is identity; staged and concatenated branch maps agree without a memory reset.
preparation_assumption: Prepreparing product input modes is a conditional open-loop representation of the source's sharp optical preparations. It does not supply apparatus authority, adaptive preparation equivalence or a physical common clock.
cavity_overlap: The previously reviewed total-N<=1 cavity/detector domain remains unchanged. Multi-bin product inputs are not automatically cavity-compatible: passive mixing can create two photons in one detected port.
assembly_guard: Before inserting a passive map ahead of a detector event, establish n_port<=1 on the transformed support. No projection, discarded multiphoton mass or hidden memory reset is allowed.
